narrative: After reviewing your application, the model calculated a 65.1% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. This low decile pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Your first-year decile of 3, compared to an accepted average of 6, also pointed toward failure, though with less influence. However, this small benefit could not override the much larger negative impact of your class rankings. The combination of the two weak deciles outweighed the LSAT’s modest support, resulting in a failure probability above 50%. To improve your chances in the future, focus on strengthening your academic record—whether through additional coursework, a post-baccalaureate program, or better study strategies—so that your class rank improves. Retaking the LSAT could also help, though your score already gave you a small advantage; the real barrier lies in your undergraduate law school performance.
